Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports direct person-to-person transfer of funds between individuals for informal transactions, remittances, and interpersonal value transfers.
Comments: BoZ Vision 2027 highlights widespread use of mobile money and states instant mobile payments were implemented, and Zambia has designated mobile payment service providers (e.g., MTN Mobile Money, Airtel Mobile Commerce, Zamtel Kwacha) enabling person-to-person transfers.
revision_notes: Fetched both originally cited BoZ sources plus AfricaNenda's SIIPS 2023 Zambia case study. The designated payment institutions page confirms licensed mobile money and payment providers. The SIIPS 2023 case study directly and authoritatively confirms that Zambia's National Financial Switch (NFS) supports P2P as a core use case (alongside P2B, G2P, cross-border), and that MTN, Airtel and Zamtel mobile money operators are integrated participants. Secondary reporting (2025/2026) corroborates continued widespread P2P mobile money use, with adoption reaching 58.5% of adults by 2025. Evidence clearly supports Value Code 2 (Yes) on the 0/1/2 scale; score confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Zambia's National Financial Switch (NFS), operated by ZECHL under Bank of Zambia oversight, supports person-to-person (P2P) transfers as one of its core use cases alongside P2B, G2P and cross-border payments. Mobile money operators including MTN Mobile Money, Airtel Money and Zamtel Kwacha are integrated participants in the NFS and are the dominant channel for P2P transfers, with mobile money adoption reaching 58.5% of adults by 2025, up from around 14% in 2015.

Definition: Whether payment system governance explicitly includes mechanisms to ensure inclusivity and represent interests of vulnerable populations, including provisions for input from all participant types, consumer representatives, small providers, or explicit financial inclusion mandates in governance documents.
Comments: AfricaNenda’s SIIPS 2023 Zambia case study notes governance inclusivity mechanisms: “The BOZ and most banking participants have a vote through their shareholding membership. Non-bank PSPs have a voice through the Payments Association of Zambia,” supporting some inclusion mechanisms but not explicit pro-poor/consumer representation (partial). BoZ Vision 2027 also explicitly targets “women, the elderly, differently abled persons, forcibly displaced persons (e.g., refugees…) and MSMEs” as inclusion priorities.
revision_notes: Fetched the SIIPS 2023 Zambia case study directly, which confirms the governance structure cited in the original comments: the NFS board is jointly owned and chaired by the Bank of Zambia and commercial banks with shareholding votes, while non-bank PSPs (which include smaller and pro-poor-oriented providers) have voice only indirectly through the Payments Association of Zambia rather than direct board representation. The full text of the BoZ National Payment Systems Vision and Strategy 2023-2027 (via a mirrored copy, as the original PDF could not be fully extracted) confirms it sets explicit targets for women, the elderly, persons with disabilities, forcibly displaced persons and MSMEs, and proposes a centralised KYC system to widen access for these groups, but these are strategic policy commitments rather than governance-structure representation. This mix of indirect participation plus policy-level inclusion targets, without direct consumer/vulnerable-group representation in governance, supports Value Code 2 (Partial) on the 0/1/2/3 scale; score confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Governance of Zambia's National Financial Switch (NFS) is a public-private partnership between the Bank of Zambia and the banking industry via ZECHL, with a board of directors on which the Bank of Zambia and member banks hold shareholding votes. Non-bank payment service providers, including smaller providers serving lower-income segments, do not sit on the ZECHL board directly but channel input through the Payments Association of Zambia, of which the Bank of Zambia is also a member. Separately, the Bank of Zambia's National Payment Systems Vision and Strategy 2023-2027 sets explicit inclusion targets for women, the elderly, persons with disabilities, forcibly displaced persons and MSMEs, and proposes a centralised KYC system to widen their access, though these remain policy commitments rather than formal governance representation mechanisms.
